name: Pizza Ortolana
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, 300 ml lukewarm water and 25 ml olive oil. Add 8 g salt and the remaining 25 ml water; knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Put in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and leave in a warm place for about 90 minutes, until roughly doubled.

Slice the eggplant and zucchini into 5-mm pieces and the peppers into strips. Brush the vegetables with 20 ml olive oil and the remaining 1 g salt. Grill in batches on a hot ridged pan for 2–3 minutes per side until marked and just tender. Spread on a plate so steam escapes. Drain and blot the mozzarella dry.

Heat the oven to 250°C, or the highest safe pizza setting, with a heavy tray or pizza stone inside for at least 25 minutes. Stir the passata with oregano and 2 g salt. Divide the risen dough in two and stretch each half on lightly floured baking paper into a roughly 28-cm round with a thicker rim.

Spread half the passata thinly on the first base, leaving the rim bare. Add half the drained mozzarella, then arrange half the grilled eggplant, zucchini and both peppers so each vegetable stays visible. Drizzle with 5 ml olive oil. Avoid piling the vegetables in one wet mound.

Slide the first pizza, paper and all, onto the hot tray. Bake 10–14 minutes until the rim is deeply golden, the base is cooked through and the cheese bubbles. Assemble and bake the second pizza in the same way with the remaining sauce, cheese, vegetables and 5 ml oil.

Scatter fresh basil over the baked pizzas and cut each into four slices. Serve two slices per person while hot. The grilled vegetables should be tender but retain their shape, and the base should not be damp.
tips: Grill and cool the vegetables before topping; raw or steaming vegetables release water and soften the crust. Check mozzarella uses microbial or vegetable rennet. Seasonal vegetables can change, but keep them pre-cooked and thoroughly drained.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
